intro.line: A rift. Heat. Sand that hums.
Another one, out of the air. The omens were right, then.
Welcome to Jamuraa, stranger. You've come at the worst possible time.
Mangara, our greatest mage, is gone. Kaervek has taken his power.
Mangara is gone. Who among you doubts that I have taken his power?

finale.line: Holy Avenger, it needs more than prayer. It needs...
Gold light. The amber cracks open. Mangara breathes. Asmira doesn't.
...but the price of Mangara's freedom was Asmira's life.
Your arrogance amazes me, Kaervek. Did you not know the price you would pay?
I knew. I just thought someone else would pay it.
He wasn't wrong, you know. Kaervek. Something is coming.
If it comes for Zhalfir, I'll hide all of it. Somewhere no war can follow.
Time may heal all wounds, but what heals time?
The isle phases out. You're standing in the sea.

villainFinale.line: Zhalfir's capital. Smoke. A throne room with nobody in it.
The end justifies the means. What do I care if I rule over the dead rather than over the living?
In the corner, Mangara still sleeps in his amber. Kaervek sits down beside it.
You were the only one who ever argued back.
Far away, something enormous turns to look at Dominaria. It doesn't care who won.

battles.title: The Lancers of Suq'Ata
battles.blurb: You land in the middle of a cavalry charge. Zhalfir's general grabs your reins before you can ask whose side you're on.

scene.line: You. Out of the sky. Can you ride?
Doesn't matter. Hold on.
Jabari! Forty lances on my left. Sixty on my right. How many have you?
Enough to be remembered.
Kaervek pays in gold, Jabari. Zhalfir pays in songs.
Command is the act of balancing on a vine and convincing others that it is firm ground.
That vine is us. Ride beside me. Never in front.

villainScene.line: The Suq'Ata trade. Silk, spice, lances. This season, lances.
Kaervek is winning. I ride with whoever is winning.
Never stop 'til you see your lance come out the other side.

hero.win: Tell Telim'Tor's paymaster he's short a general.

villain.loss: Zhalfir pays in songs. Write me a short one.

battles.title: Teferi's Isle
battles.blurb: Jabari sends you to Zhalfir's court mage for help. The court mage is a thousand years old, lives on an island that isn't always there, and wants to play first.

scene.line: You walked straight onto the isle. Most people need three tries.
The island phases. Here, then not. Like most of my friends.
Can you prepare for the unexpected? No, you cannot. You can prepare only to be surprised.
Jabari wants my help with Kaervek. I want to know if you're worth my time.
So. A game. Your cards will step out of time and back. Try to keep up.
I had a teacher who played like this once. He never said sorry either.

villainScene.line: A planeswalker? Here? Oh, this is going to be fun.
Let's see how you play when your army keeps disappearing.

villain.low: Careless, like a child with fire, so was I with time.
villain.loss: Good. Now I'm worried about Kaervek, not you.

battles.title: The Song of Blood
battles.blurb: A Femeref village goes quiet at sunset. Something is singing in the grass. Rashida has been waiting for it for three nights.

scene.line: Don't light a fire. He's drawn to it.
He hunts at dusk. He kills while you're busy.
So we'll be busy on HIS turn.
Tell me... have you ever sung the Song of Blood?
Once. I don't like the tune.
Death is not a debt I am yet willing to pay.
Hold your fire until he's mid-leap.

villainScene.line: Kaervek calls us night stalkers. "Willing tools."
He thinks the swamp takes orders. The swamp takes everything.
Tonight, the village dances.

hero.low: I've been bitten by worse. Dragons, mostly.

battles.title: The Amber Prison
battles.blurb: Deep in the Mwonvuli jungle, Mangara hangs inside a block of amber like a fly. The jungle's empress has been told to keep him there.

scene.line: There he is. Mangara. He looks... asleep.
He is not asleep. He is kept. As you will be, if you touch it.
Jolrael. You hid from Zhalfir for centuries. Why come out for Kaervek?
I have hidden from the machinations of Zhalfir for centuries. Why should I join your campaign?
Kaervek promised the Mwonvuli would be left alone. Zhalfir never did.
Kaervek imprisoned Mangara out of jealousy, but he taints Jamuraa simply out of spite.
He'll keep his promise to you exactly as long as it's useful.
I need no army. I have Jamuraa.

villainScene.line: Every hundred years, a Zhalfirin army marches through my trees.
Every hundred years, my trees are fewer.
Kaervek swore by fire he would never set foot here. I chose the lesser fire.

after.line: Asmira's prayers crack the amber. They don't break it.
Asmira's prayers alone should have freed Mangara from the amber prison...

hero.low: Faith is my shield, and hope is my armor; I am vulnerable only to myself.
hero.win: We're coming back for you, Mangara.

villain.big: What need have I for cavalry when I can have horse and rider both in one?
villain.loss: Go, then. I didn't see you.

battles.title: The Last Library
battles.blurb: Kaervek's ally has come for Femeref's library. She doesn't want to burn it. She wants to rewrite it.

scene.line: Femeref was guided by the wisdom of the Council of Voices. But in one terrible instant, they were slain.
Their names are in this library. If it falls, they die twice.
Loreweaver. I don't burn books. Barbarians burn books.
I write upon clean white parchment with a sharp quill and the blood of my students.
Let me write your ending. It will be beautiful.
Every spell she casts is a sentence. We say no to every sentence.

villainScene.line: History belongs to whoever holds the pen.
When I am done, Femeref will remember Kaervek as its saviour. And me as its scholar.
I no longer believe in a final resting place.

villain.big: The flesh is a casket for the soul.

battles.title: Prosperity
battles.blurb: On your way to the front you stop in a Suq'Ata bazaar for water. You leave owing a merchant a duel, two goats and an apology. His machines make everyone draw. He's the one holding the fireball.

scene.line: Friend! Stranger! Friend-stranger! You look thirsty. And rich.
Water, one coin. Water that heals, two coins.
Eternal life or your money back.
No? You said no? To Pashad?
Nobody says no to Pashad. It is very bad for business.
Very well. A wager. If I win, you buy everything.
My machines are very fair. Everybody draws. EVERYBODY.
Everybody draws! Everybody prospers! Mostly me.

villainScene.line: Wealth is a good thing, compared to poverty. Your food is better, your robes are softer.
The war is terrible for business. Except the business of war, which is wonderful.
A planeswalker customer! Do they pay in other worlds' coins? Let's find out.

after.line: A map to Kaervek's camp. Mostly accurate. For you, half price.
It's entirely accurate. That's what worries me. Why does a merchant have it?

villain.big: Look at all these cards! Everybody gets some!
villain.low: This is not how the deal was described to me.
villain.win: Two goats. And the apology, in writing.
villain.loss: Fine! Free water. Don't tell anyone.

battles.title: Fireblast
battles.blurb: The map was accurate. So was the ambush. Kaervek's embermages hold the road to his camp, and they don't negotiate. The original red curve deck.

scene.line: Common soldiers can't understand what a sidar knows: the enemy can be a resource.
So, embermage. Surrender, and your fire serves Zhalfir.
AAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!
...I'll take that as no.
Fast, then. We win before she finishes screaming.

villainScene.line: Comfortable even in a furnace? I've never met one who'd accept my wager.
Kaervek promised the Burning Isles would never kneel to Zhalfir again.
I was born on a volcano. I know exactly how long a mountain can wait.
Not one day more.

hero.big: Do not underestimate the power of many against one.
hero.low: My soldiers fought without hesitation, died without doubt.

villain.low: I have one more. I always have one more.

battles.title: Kaervek's Torch
battles.blurb: Three nations that have hated each other for centuries ride together into Kaervek's camp. He's been expecting them. He seems almost pleased.

scene.line: We are to be bound together as the reeds of a basket.
Suq'Ata believe in trade; Femeref, alms; Zhalfirins, steel. Be warned, Kaervek. Now we are joined.
Joined. Good. You see? It only took a war.
You murdered the Council of Voices.
The council argued for eleven years about a well.
Something is coming, Holy Avenger. Not me. Something older.
The secrets of Phyrexia are expensive. You will pay in brass and bone, steel and sinew.
When it comes, a continent of councils dies. A fist survives.
And you're the fist.
Someone has to be.
Then let someone else be the hand that opens.

villainScene.line: They call me merciless. They have never seen what is coming.
Kill a creature, destroy the present. Kill the land, destroy the future.
I'll burn Zhalfir down to the stone, and build something that survives the burning.
Since I cannot stop death, I choose to stop life.

hero.start: Tread upon the meek, and they shall wound your feet.
hero.big: This is a war without neutrality.
hero.low: I've dreamt of a second harvest but fear I will not see it.

villain.big: Only fools believe they will face my armies but once.
villain.low: If it is weak, either kill it or ignore it.
villain.win: Jamuraa will look to only one leader.
villain.loss: You'll wish you'd let me win. When it comes.

half.line: I have seen the horrors Kaervek has freed. My betrayal is certain, but of Kaervek or of Jamuraa, I cannot say.
